items.prompt: White to move. One white piece is attacked and no white piece defends it. Tap that piece.

claims.statement: The knight on e4 is White's only loose piece.

hints: Look at what the black knight on f6 attacks.
It attacks the square e4, where a white piece stands.
The knight on e4.
items.explain: The black knight on f6 attacks the knight on e4, and no white piece defends that square. White must move it, defend it or trade it. That choice is move five.

items.prompt: Black to move. The white knight on g5 attacks two black pawns. Tap the pawn that only the king defends.

claims.statement: One white piece (the knight) attacks f7.
One black piece (the king) defends f7.
Two black pieces (rook and knight) defend h7.
A black pawn stands on f7.

hints: The knight on g5 attacks f7 and h7. Count the defenders of each.
The pawn on h7 has a rook and a knight behind it.
f7: the king on e8 is its only defender.
items.explain: The knight on g5 attacks f7 and h7. The pawn on h7 is defended by the rook on h8 and the knight on f6. The pawn on f7 is defended only by the king on e8, so f7 is the weaker target.

items.prompt: White to move. Black's pawn attacks the knight on g5. Find the move that is within 40 centipawns of the engine's top move (depth 16).

claims.statement: The retreat to f3 is within 40 cp of the engine's top move (depth 16).
The retreat to h3 is at least 30 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).
Taking on f7 is at least 100 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: The knight is attacked by a pawn and cannot stay on g5.
One retreat keeps every piece and returns the knight to a central square.
The knight on g5 goes back to f3.
items.explain: The pawn on h6 attacks the knight and the knight is defended only by the bishop on c1. Retreating to f3 keeps all the material and brings the knight back towards the centre. The retreat to h3 also keeps the piece but puts it at the edge, and taking on f7 gives up a knight for a pawn. Engine, depth 16: the retreat to f3 is the top move; the other two are clearly behind.

feedback_by_move.g5f7: This gives a knight for a pawn: the king simply takes. The next boards show what White hopes to get for it, and the engine's verdict.
feedback_by_move.g5h3: The knight keeps its life but stands at the edge, far from the centre.

items.prompt: Black to move on move five. Three of these four replies are within 40 centipawns of the engine's top move (depth 16); one is clearly worse. Which one is the worse reply?

claims.statement: ...c5, ...h6 and ...Bf5 are each within 40 cp of the top move (depth 16).
...Be6 is at least 150 cp worse than the best move.

hints: Black wants to keep the pieces safe and develop. Check which squares the white knight attacks.
Look at where each bishop or pawn move puts a piece, and whether the knight on g5 can attack it.
items.explain: ...c5, ...h6 and ...Bf5 keep Black's pieces safe and develop or fight for d4. ...Be6 puts the bishop on a square the knight attacks; after the trade on e6 Black's pawns are broken and the king is exposed. Engine, depth 16: the three moves are within 40 centipawns of the top move; ...Be6 is at least 150 behind. Several other quiet replies are also within 40, so this item lists only some of them.

feedback_by_move.c8e6: The knight on g5 attacks e6. After the trade on e6 Black's pawns are broken and the king is exposed.

items.prompt: Black to move. White's knight has just taken on f7. Tap every black queen, rook or pawn that it attacks.

claims.statement: The knight on f7 attacks exactly these squares.
A black queen stands on d8.
A black rook stands on h8.
A black pawn stands on h6.
d6 is empty.
e5 is empty.
g5 is empty.

hints: Count the squares a knight attacks from f7, then see which of them hold black units.
Two of the six squares hold the queen and a rook; a third holds a pawn.
d8, h8 and h6.
items.explain: From f7 the knight attacks d8, h8, d6, h6, e5 and g5. The black queen stands on d8, a rook on h8 and a pawn on h6. The squares d6, e5 and g5 are empty.

items.prompt: Black to move. The knight on f7 attacks the queen and a rook. Find the move within 40 centipawns of the engine's top move (depth 16).

claims.statement: Taking the knight with the king is the engine's top move (depth 16).
Moving the queen to d5 is at least 400 cp worse than the best move.
Developing the bishop to g4 is at least 400 cp worse than the best move.
Developing the bishop to f5 is at least 400 cp worse than the best move.

hints: Two black pieces are attacked. Can you remove the attacker instead of moving them?
Is the white knight defended by anything?
The king on e8 takes the knight.
items.explain: Nothing defends the knight on f7 and the king stands next to it, so the king captures it and both threats vanish at once. Any other move leaves the queen or the rook to be taken. Engine, depth 16: the alternatives tried (Qd5, Bg4, Bf5) each lose at least four pawns more.

feedback_by_move.d8d5: The queen leaves, but the knight takes the rook on h8.
feedback_by_move.c8g4: The bishop attacks the white queen, but the knight takes the black queen first.
feedback_by_move.c8f5: The knight takes the queen on d8; the bishop move gained nothing.

items.prompt: White to move after 6...Kxf7. Find a move within 40 centipawns of the engine's top move (depth 16).

claims.statement: Nf3 and Bc4+ are each within 40 cp of the top move (depth 16).
Qh5+ is at least 500 cp worse than the best move.

hints: White is a piece down. Which move develops with a threat or a check?
The king is on f7; the bishop's diagonal to it is open.
Nf3 develops, Bc4+ gives check: either one.
items.explain: The knight on f3 develops and eyes e5. The bishop on c4 develops with check, because the diagonal to the king on f7 is open. Both are developing moves that keep the initiative. Engine, depth 16: both are within 40 centipawns of the top move.

feedback_by_move.d1h5: The knight on f6 guards h5, so Nxh5 wins the queen for nothing.

items.prompt: White to move. Black's king has lost the pawn cover on the g-file. Find the strongest move: it is a check.

claims.statement: Qg3+ is the engine's top move (depth 16).
After Qg3+ the engine value is at least +5 pawns for White (depth 16).

hints: Look for a check that attacks the king along an open file.
The queen can check on the g-file.
Qg3+.
items.explain: The pawn on g7 has gone, so the g-file is open in front of the king, and the queen on f3 can swing to g3 with check. Black's king has no pawn cover and White's knight on e5 is ready to jump to f7. Engine, depth 16: Qg3+ is the top move and White is well ahead afterwards.

items.prompt: Black to move after 7.Nf3. Three of these four moves stay within 70 centipawns of the engine's top move (depth 16); one loses at least 150 (about a pawn and a half). Which move loses?

claims.statement: ...c5, ...e6 and ...Bf5 are each within 70 cp of the top move (depth 16).
...Bg4 is at least 150 cp worse than the best move.

hints: The king is on f7. Which of these moves leaves a piece where a check can hit two things?
A knight check on e5 would hit the king and one more piece.
items.explain: ...c5, ...e6 and ...Bf5 develop without leaving a piece where a knight check hits it. ...Bg4 puts the bishop on a square that the knight on e5 attacks with check, and White wins it (two attackers, one defender). Engine, depth 16: the first three are within 70 centipawns of the top move; ...Bg4 is at least 150 behind it.

feedback_by_move.c8g4: Ne5+ gives check and attacks the bishop on g4, so the bishop is lost.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the move within 40 centipawns of the engine's top move (depth 16).

claims.statement: Bc4+ is the engine's top move (depth 16).
Bd3 is at least 100 cp worse than the best move.

hints: The black king is on g8 and the a2-g8 diagonal is open.
One bishop move develops with check.
Bc4+.
items.explain: The bishop on c4 gives check and develops, keeping the black king under pressure. The quiet Bd3 offers a trade of bishops, which helps the side that is a piece ahead. Engine, depth 16: Bc4+ is the top move; Bd3 is at least a pawn behind it.

feedback_by_move.f1d3: The bishop offers a trade; Black accepts happily, because trades help the side that is a piece ahead.

items.prompt: Black to move on move five. After which of these four moves is the square g5 attacked by a black piece?

claims.statement: After ...h6 one black piece (the pawn) attacks g5.
After ...c5 no black piece attacks g5.
After ...Bf5 no black piece attacks g5.
After ...e6 no black piece attacks g5.

hints: Which Black piece could attack a knight on g5?
A pawn attacks diagonally forward.
The pawn on h7 moves to h6.
items.explain: A pawn attacks the squares diagonally in front of it. After ...h6 the pawn attacks g5. The other three moves leave g5 unattacked.

items.prompt: White gives the knight for the pawn on f7. Is that sacrifice sound?

claims.statement: Taking on f7 is at least 150 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: Sound here means the engine does not rate it clearly worse than the retreat. Engines count in centipawns: 100 is about one pawn; clearly worse means at least 150 below the best move (depth 16).
Count what White gives and what White takes.
A knight is worth about three pawns and the move takes one.
No: it gives up a knight for a pawn and the compensation does not make up the difference.
items.explain: White gives a knight (about three pawns, or 300 centipawns) and takes a pawn, so it starts two pawns down. The engine agrees that the sacrifice is clearly worse than the retreat, so it is not sound.

items.prompt: White's knight stands on f7. Does it attack the black queen?

claims.statement: The knight on f7 attacks exactly these squares.
The black queen stands on d8.

hints: Which squares does a knight on f7 attack?
d8 is one of them.
Yes: the queen stands on d8.
items.explain: The queen stands on d8, one of the six squares the knight attacks from f7.

items.prompt: Same position, but Black's queen stands on c7. Does the knight on f7 attack the queen?

claims.statement: The knight on f7 attacks exactly these squares.
The black queen stands on c7.

hints: Which squares does a knight on f7 attack?
Is c7 one of them?
No: c7 is not among the six squares.
items.explain: The queen on c7 is not on any of the six squares the knight attacks, so the fork loses its queen target.

items.prompt: Same position as the first, but Black's light bishop stands on f5. Does the knight on f7 attack the queen?

claims.statement: The knight on f7 attacks exactly these squares.
The black queen stands on d8.

hints: Which squares does a knight on f7 attack?
Does the bishop's square matter?
Yes: the queen still stands on d8.
items.explain: The bishop on f5 is not on any of the six squares, so it changes nothing. The queen still stands on d8.
